Deforestation & Land-Cover Change

Compare land-cover dates, trace forest loss and summarize transitions into other land uses.

Watch the Video ↗All Use Cases ↗

Where has forest cover changed, and what land-cover classes replaced it?

The video follows land-cover changes between 1992 and 2022. It uses class metadata to translate raster codes into named land-cover categories, making changes easier to interpret.

After aligning the data, the analysis builds transition summaries and distinguishes forest-to-cropland change from other forest-loss pathways. Mapped classes and tabular exports keep the geography connected to the quantitative result.

From question to analysis

Data and inputs

  • Categorical land-cover rasters for the comparison dates
  • Class definitions and metadata
  • A study boundary and an area-calculation reference system

Analysis described in the video

  1. Inspect the dates, class definitions and spatial alignment.
  2. Identify forest classes and compare them with the later land-cover categories.
  3. Calculate transitions and summarize their areas or proportions.
  4. Map the different loss pathways and export the results.

Understand the output

Outputs described

  • Forest-loss maps separated by destination class
  • Land-cover transition summaries and exportable tables

What to review

  • Check that class definitions are comparable across dates.
  • Review alignment and area units before interpreting change totals.
